_note: Prototype 4: one lesson in the new eight-step daily loop, for the sound f. Not part of curriculum.json; the 13 real lessons are unchanged. Scripts may hold {blend:fit} (the stretched word, built by slowSounds), {blend:@} (the word on screen) and {sound:f} (soundText). Tips are CURRICULUM.md section 13, verbatim.
title: New lesson: f

steps.name: Sound Warm-up
steps.about: Blend sounds into a word, then break a word into sounds.
steps.tip: Sound games work noticeably better when letters are involved. Say "sun," then have your child find the letter that makes the first sound.

steps.name: Quick Review
steps.about: Say old sounds and read old words before hearing the answer.
steps.tip: Children learn best by seeing or hearing it done first. If your child is stuck on a sound, say it first, then invite them: "You try!"

steps.name: New Sound: f
steps.about: Meet f: the flower picture, the mouth, then say it and trace it.
steps.tip: Say /m/ as "mmm," not "muh." Extra "uh" sounds make blending harder: "buh-a-tuh" doesn't sound like "bat." Keep stop sounds short and crisp, like a tiny hiccup.

steps.name: Blend It
steps.about: I do, then we do: blend fit, fat and if together.
steps.tip: Children blend better when sounds are stretched together ("mmmaaat") than chopped apart ("m... a... t"). Chopping makes them forget the first sound by the time they reach the last.

steps.name: Read It
steps.about: Your child reads six words alone; you judge each one.
steps.tip: How you correct matters. Point to the exact letter, say its sound, and have your child reread the word. That works better than a general "try again."

steps.name: Build It
steps.about: Spell with letter tiles, then change one letter at a time.
steps.tip: Spelling practice makes children better readers, not just better spellers. Say "map" and have your child build it with magnet letters.

steps.name: Read a Story
steps.about: A three-line story with only the sounds your child knows.
steps.tip: Rereading the same short story builds fluency. Read a page aloud first, then let your child read it 3 or 4 times over a few days.

scripts.a: Play the blend, or say it yourself: {blend:@}. Your child slides a finger under the letters and says it with you, smooth and joined. Then ask, "What word?" Let your child answer first.
scripts.b: Say the word slowly: {blend:@}. Your child taps a box for each sound, and the letters appear one by one. Let your child try first; if they are stuck, say the sounds together.

scripts.letters: Your child tries first: they say the sound before the app plays it. Tap Got it if they know it. Stuck? Tap Help, play the sound, and say it together. Still stuck? Say it yourself, then have your child say it after you. The card comes back once at the end. Keep p and t quick, with no uh.
scripts.words: Ask your child to read the word. If they know some of the letters, sound it out together. Still stuck? Read it yourself, then have your child say it after you. Tap Got it if your child read it. Tap Help if not: tap the tricky letter, play its sound, then the whole word. Your child blends it again.
scripts.wagons: Say: "Say the sound first, then find it!" Your child says the sound of the letter on the card. Then your child taps every wagon with that letter. If they are stuck, say the sound together.
scripts.wagonsGist: Say it first, then find it.

scripts.meet: This is f. The stem, the two leaves and the flower head make the letter. I do: tap Hear it and listen. We do: say {sound:f} together, a long breath through your teeth.
scripts.mouth: I do: put your top teeth on your bottom lip and blow: {sound:f}. Not fuh. We do: do it together. You do: your child tries it alone. They can feel the air on a hand.
scripts.say: You do: your child says the sound three times. Tap a dot after each one. Tap Hear it to play the recording. If they are stuck, say it together.
scripts.trace: I do: draw the letter while your child watches. Say {sound:f} as you trace. We do: trace it together. You do: your child traces it alone. Start at the dot and follow the arrow. It does not have to look right yet. Your child can still move on.

newsound.mouthLine: Top teeth on your bottom lip, and blow: {sound:f}. Not fuh.

scripts.ido: I do: say the word slowly and smoothly while the letters light up: {blend:@}. Your child watches and listens.
scripts.wedo: We do: slide your fingers along the letters together and say it together: {blend:@}. Then say the whole word fast and ask, "What word?"
scripts.wedoGist: We do: slide and say it.

scripts.read: Ask your child to read the word. If they know some of the letters, sound it out together. Still stuck? Read it yourself, then have your child say it after you. Tap Got it if your child read it. Tap Help if not: tap the tricky letter, play its sound, then the whole word. Your child blends it again. A missed word comes back once at the end.

scripts.first: The phone says the word. Say it slowly together: {blend:@}. Then your child taps tiles to fill the boxes from left to right. To send a tile back, tap its box.
scripts.chain: Say: "Change one letter to make @." Do not point to the letter. Your child listens for the sound that changed. This trains children to look at every letter, not just the first.

question.right: Yes! It is a fat map.

scripts.line: Ask your child to read the line. If they know some of the letters, sound it out together. Still stuck? Read it yourself, then have your child say it after you. Tap Got it if your child read the line. Tap Help if not: tap the tricky word, play its sounds (you say a heart word whole). Your child reads the whole line again.
scripts.page: Your child reads the whole story again, a little faster. Tap Hear the story first, to hear it read smoothly. Then your child rereads it. Tap Next for a question.
scripts.question: Ask: "What is fat?" Your child taps a picture. This checks meaning, not reading.

celebrate.heading: You read your first f words!
celebrate.didYouKnow: Short, spaced practice beats long sessions. Ten to fifteen minutes a day works better than an hour on the weekend.
